sections.html:
In Seattle you can list through an agent, sell the house on your own, or accept a cash bid from someone who buys it as-is. The pace depends on what shape the house is in, whether renters occupy it, and how much you are prepared to fix up first.

The market is expensive, and most households rent. About 784,777 people lived here on July 1, 2025, up from 737,015 in the 2020 census, and owners occupy only 43.7 percent of homes. Figures for 2020 to 2024 put the median owner-occupied home at $938,600, median gross rent at $2,030 a month and median household income at $123,860. There are 363,466 households of about 2.00 people each, and the mean commute is 26.0 minutes.

Plenty of local sellers own a rental, inherited a house, or hold an older place that needs work. Each situation has its own rules, explained below.

Light rail has also changed which addresses feel convenient. The 1 Line reached Northgate in October 2021 and Lynnwood in August 2024, so a house within walking distance of a station can be worth pointing out in the listing.

sections.h2: Hills, water and the disclosure form
sections.html:
The city lies on slopes between Puget Sound and Lake Washington, in earthquake country, with a rainy season that runs October through March. Roofs, basements and drainage take a beating, and the state's seller form probes every one of them.

Sample questions: Did the roof leak in the past five years? Has the basement flooded or leaked? Has the lot settled, slipped or slid? Was there material damage from an earthquake, flood or landslide? Whatever you leave out, an inspector is likely to find, so tell the buyer first.

Hills are part of the city's identity. Capitol Hill, First Hill, Beacon Hill, Queen Anne, Magnolia and West Seattle are the usual list, and the highest point inside city limits reaches 520 feet above sea level at Myrtle Reservoir Park in High Point. Slope matters to a buyer: ask yourself what your lot has done in heavy rain, and keep any geotechnical or drainage paperwork handy.

The magnitude 6.8 Nisqually earthquake on February 28, 2001, did heavy damage in Pioneer Square, which stands on reclaimed land, and the Seattle Fault runs just south of downtown. A house with a retrofit, a new foundation or a chimney repair should have that work documented in your sale folder.

If a neighbor's slope, a retaining wall or a shared drainage line affects your lot, mention it on the form too. Buyers forgive known issues more readily than surprises.

sections.h2: Excise tax and what you owe at closing
sections.html:
For most Seattle sellers the excise tax on real estate is the biggest closing cost. Washington expects the seller to pay it. When a seller does not, responsibility shifts to the buyer and an unpaid amount may turn into a lien. The state's share is tiered, with each slice of the sale price taxed at its own rate:

  • 1.1 percent applies up to $525,000.
  • 1.28 percent covers the part between $525,000 and $1,525,000.
  • 2.75 percent covers the part between $1,525,000 and $3,025,000.
  • 3 percent applies to everything above $3,025,000.

For sales beginning January 1, 2027 the tiers break at $551,000, $1,551,000 and $3,051,000, and the four rates stay the same. A local rate comes on top, listed in the Department of Revenue's local rate table. To find the local rate for a Seattle address, ask your closing agent or the King County treasurer.

Payment goes to the county treasurer by the sale date, defined by the state as the day the deed is notarized. After a month of nonpayment, interest accrues at the 6 percent the Department of Revenue lists for 2026 and 2027. The state can audit a sale, so keep your records for at least four years. Your parcel's property tax balance and due dates are available from the King County treasurer.

If the property is improved residential land, you owe the buyer a completed disclosure statement, unless the buyer waives it or the transfer is exempt. The deadline in RCW 64.06.020 is five business days after both parties accept a written purchase contract, though they may agree to a different period.

From delivery, the buyer has three business days to rescind in writing, or may give that right up. Only the seller signs the form, and it is no warranty. Topics include title, water, sewer, structure, systems, homeowners' associations and environmental conditions, with a reminder about carbon monoxide alarms and a smoke detector.

Give construction history the most attention. The form wants to know about conversions, additions and remodels, and whether every building permit and final inspection was obtained. Did you finish a basement or add a bedroom years back? Find those records before you answer. The Seattle Department of Construction and Inspections can tell you what is on file for your address.

sections.h2: A rough timeline for a quick Seattle sale
sections.html:
Fast sales in Seattle start with homework done before any offer lands. One workable order:

  1. Settle the tenant question first. A rented single-family house with a tenant who must leave needs 90 days of written notice, so that clock comes before listing.
  2. Gather permit papers and inspection records so the state form can be completed in one sitting.
  3. Request the tax balance from the county treasurer and ask your closing agent which local excise rate fits your address.
  4. Once a contract is signed, hand the buyer your disclosure statement inside five business days.
  5. Allow the buyer three business days to rescind, then proceed to title work, the notarized deed and recording.

No repair crew is needed for any of this. A cash buyer will take a worn house as-is, with the offer already adjusted.

With a tenant in the house, two rule sets apply: Seattle's rental registration program and the state's process for ending a tenancy. The city's Rental Registration and Inspection Ordinance wants a rental registered once it has a tenant, and a short-term rental that is not the operator's primary residence must register before it is listed. Registrations are good for two years.

City inspector, each additional unit$52.50

A property is selected for inspection once in its first five years, then faces a 10 percent chance of selection again in the next five. At least 60 days are allowed to complete it, and tenants must be told at least two days before the visit. Typical failures include absent smoke or carbon monoxide detectors, missing handrails and exposed wiring. The RRIO helpline number is (206) 684-4110.

A tenanted single-family house can be cleared for sale under RCW 59.18.650, provided the tenant gets 90 days of written notice. Listing at a reasonable price within 30 days after move-out shows the sale is real. Put the house back up for rent, or take it off the market, within 90 days and the law presumes you never meant to sell. Improper removal costs the landlord the larger of the tenant's damages or three times monthly rent, with attorney fees and court costs added.

sections.h2: When a cash sale makes sense
sections.html:
Cash is often right for a fixer-upper, an estate house, a rental whose tenants are hard to manage, or a hard move date. Before saying yes, work through this list:

  • Learn who pays the excise tax and any title or escrow fees, and get that in writing.
  • Fix the closing day, and ask whether the buyer accepts the house with tenants staying.
  • Compare the bid with what similar houses nearby sold for lately.
  • If the house has been rented, check where you stand with the rental registration program.
  • Collect permits for additions, because the disclosure form still asks about them.

After you say yes, escrow opens and a title search begins. Any mortgage is cleared from proceeds, and you sign the deed before a notary. The county receives the affidavit and tax, and money is released after recording. Nobody orders an appraisal or lender review, so title work and your own calendar mostly set the date.

faqs.q: Who pays the real estate excise tax when I sell a house in Seattle?
faqs.a: The seller, in the usual case. Skip it and the buyer becomes liable, with a possible lien on the property. The county treasurer collects by the sale date, at state rates from 1.1 percent to 3 percent plus a local rate.

faqs.q: Do I have to give a buyer a disclosure statement in Seattle?
faqs.a: In most improved residential sales, yes. RCW 64.06.020 gives you five business days after the contract is accepted, and the buyer then has three business days to rescind in writing. A waiver or exemption changes this.

faqs.q: Do I need to register my Seattle rental before I sell it?
faqs.a: Yes, once a tenant lives there. A registration lasts two years, and being late or skipping an inspection costs $150 per day for 10 days, then $500 per day.

faqs.q: Can I sell a Seattle house that has tenants in it?
faqs.a: Yes. Buyers can accept the lease as written. If you need the house empty first, RCW 59.18.650 asks for 90 days of written notice and a genuine listing effort within 30 days of move-out.

faqs.q: What if my Seattle house has an addition built without a permit?
faqs.a: The sale can still go ahead. Answer the permit question on the state form truthfully, and check with the Seattle Department of Construction and Inspections for records on your address.
